newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian investment firm buys Lithuanian broker.
newsitem.headline: Estonian investment firm buys Lithuanian broker.

text.p: Leading Estonian investment company Talinvest said on Thursday that it had bought 87 percent of Lithuanian brokerage Suprema to create an investment bank covering the Baltic region.
"Talinvest's acquisition is part of a long-term strategy to create a strong presence in all three Baltic countries," Talinvest said in a statement.
Talinvest, which had non-consolidated assets of 144 million kroons as of the end of November 1996, last year became a member of the Riga stock exchange.
"This allows the new investment bank to offer a full range of brokerage and corporate finance services for the first time for its clients in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania," Talinvest added.
Talinvest said that Suprema trade accounted for around 25 percent of turnover on the Lithuanian stock market.
The move by Talinvest is part of an increasing trend for regionalisation in Baltic financial markets, spearheaded by Estonian companies.
The Estonian financial sector is seen as more advanced than its Latvian and Lithuanian counterparts.
Leading Estonian bank Hansapank led the way last year by buying a Latvian bank. Fellow bank Tallinna Pank has just completed a deal to buy 20 percent of Latvian Saules Bank.
